controls.reason: The statement is a timing-and-documentation requirement, and the authenticated release record contains both criteria with an effective timestamp before launch.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried adding criteria after launch or leaving one criterion empty; both fail the ordering and nonempty-field checks. The rule does not require judging whether the chosen criteria are wise.

controls.reason: The control requires that rollback be rehearsed, and a completed authenticated execution bound to the exact artifact, configuration, and procedure proves that occurrence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A rehearsal against a different artifact, stale configuration, or different procedure fails the binding. An unsuccessful rehearsal is still a rehearsal; readiness or successful rollback is a separate stronger claim.

controls.reason: A release manifest can omit database or event changes, and passing approved tests does not prove semantic compatibility for every consumer, stored state, ordering, and mixed-version path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The release changes an event field through runtime configuration but omits it from the manifest. All inventoried schema tests pass, while the previous artifact crashes on the changed event.

controls.reason: Exact prior artifact and configuration identifiers are bound to the previous successful deployment, and current retrieval plus immutable digest checks decide availability completely.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a similarly named artifact, corrupted object, or missing configuration; each fails the exact version or digest check. Whether rollback will succeed is outside this availability-only statement.

controls.reason: An approved scenario matrix can be arbitrarily incomplete, and execution records do not establish that traffic shifting and load-balancer behavior were meaningfully tested across failure, drain, health, stickiness, and connection cases.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The matrix tests only a 1% shift of one HTTP request and passes, while long-lived connections are dropped during a real 50% shift. The proposal still reports every declared scenario executed.

controls.reason: The release inventory cannot independently prove every affected application cache, browser cache, edge cache, CDN key, region, and variant is included.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A localized CDN cache is affected but omitted from the inventory and has no invalidation plan. Every listed surface has all plan fields, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The DNS change inventory can omit console, registrar, delegated-zone, provider-generated, and manual changes, allowing unplanned changes to evade the record check.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An operator changes a delegated CNAME directly at the DNS provider without adding it to the release inventory. All inventoried changes have complete plans, so the checker passes.

controls.reason: The certificate-change and endpoint inventories can omit certificates, alternate hostnames, termination layers, and manually managed endpoints.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A certificate is replaced on an unlisted legacy hostname with no rollback plan or monitoring. Every inventoried change and endpoint satisfies both clauses, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The deployment orchestrator cannot prove completeness for manual, out-of-band, privileged, provider-side, or audit-bypassing actions; its manifest is circular evidence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An administrator changes a production flag directly after pausing audit collection. Every orchestrated action has an audit event, so the clauses pass while that deployment action is not auditable.

controls.reason: A digest self-reported by a deployed instance is not authoritative proof of the bytes actually executing unless a trusted attestation and complete instance inventory are defined.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A compromised instance runs modified code but returns the expected digest from a configured endpoint. Every reported digest matches the manifest, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The proposal has no independent complete inventory of deployed targets, and runtime queries may omit cached, process-local, regional, or manually overridden configuration.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A forgotten instance runs an old feature-flag cache but is absent from the queried target list. All queried targets match the manifest, so the checker passes.

controls.reason: The release manifest cannot prove it includes every target database, schema object, out-of-band migration, and provider-managed schema change.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A tenant database is omitted and misses a migration. Every database named in the manifest has matching fingerprints and history, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The capability matrix controls applicability and can omit real login, logout, recovery, federation, break-glass, or privileged-authentication variants.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A privileged recovery path bypasses MFA but is omitted from the matrix. Every declared scenario passes, so the proposal passes while privileged authentication is not fully tested.

controls.reason: The original says multiple roles and tenants, and the bounded suite requires at least two of each with versioned allow and deny expectations and successful execution.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a single role, a single tenant, or allow-only cases; each fails the explicit cardinality or matrix requirements. Exhaustive testing of every role is not stated by this control.

controls.reason: The claimed inventory cannot exhaust dynamic routes, administrative variants, workers, schedulers, alternate accounts, and paths created outside the discovery source.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A database-scheduled worker is absent from the capability inventory and fails after deployment. Every listed path has a successful result, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: An endpoint inventory can omit hostnames, origins, ports, protocols, alternate routes, and provider endpoints, leaving their TLS and HTTP policy unverified.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A legacy public hostname with permissive CORS is absent from the inventory. Every listed endpoint matches policy, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The approved cache contract can omit variation, authorization, stale-content, multi-region, and failure behaviors, so a finite request sequence need not verify the broad behavior.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The contract tests hit, miss, and purge for public content but omits authorization variation; private responses are cached across users. Every declared scenario passes.

controls.reason: The production-monitor inventory can omit alert rules, synthetic journeys, routes, regions, and monitors created in other systems, so trigger success covers only discovered objects.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A paging alert in a secondary monitoring account is missing and routes nowhere. Every inventoried alert and synthetic probe passes, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The statement requires a comparison, not a favorable result, and the rollout record fixes cohorts, window, formulas, and metrics before authenticated observations are compared.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a missing cohort, metric, or comparison result; each fails. A statistically weak experiment may still be a comparison, because significance and decision quality are not promised here.

controls.reason: Which analytics and business indicators are applicable is a contextual release decision, and the plan may omit a harmed business outcome while all declared comparisons pass.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The release breaks renewals, but renewal rate is omitted from the approved indicator list. Every declared metric meets its range, so the proposal passes while a key business indicator was not verified.

controls.reason: The approved handoff manifest defines the exact expected telemetry, document versions, recipients, and authenticated delivery or access evidence, matching the receipt claim.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried giving support an old document, omitting a recipient, or granting no telemetry access; each fails the version, recipient, or evidence join. Whether the materials are useful is outside this receipt-only rule.

controls.reason: The signed plan defines both the agreed interval and the precise heightened-monitor set, while configuration and telemetry prove every monitor remained active throughout it.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a monitor disabled for five minutes or a shorter interval; continuous time-aligned records expose both failures. The term heightened is not invented by the checker because the plan defines the exact set.

controls.reason: Quantifying only over recorded threshold crossings is circular because monitoring gaps, delayed samples, aggregation, and omitted rollout events can hide a real crossing or later expansion.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A metric crosses the stop threshold during a telemetry outage, so no crossing is recorded and rollout expansion continues. The every-recorded-crossing check is vacuously true.

controls.reason: The rule is an exact recording requirement, and one authenticated allowed state with actor, timestamp, and release binding fully decides it.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried two conflicting final states, a missing actor, or a decision bound to another release; each fails. Whether the accountable decision was correct is outside the statement.

controls.reason: The final release record cannot prove it contains every real deferred observation and temporary control, so omitted items evade follow-up scheduling.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A temporary firewall exception is created during launch but omitted from the final record. Every recorded temporary item has a follow-up date, so the proposal passes while the exception has none.
